record.text: Changing normalise()'s exact output would break the three downstream systems' reconciliation against records already written.
record.source: Stated reason for the freeze. Code evidence against it: all three consumers in downstream.py call normalise(x).strip(), and test_downstream.py pins already-stripped values, so stripping inside normalise() changes nothing they receive. Not marked verified-false because 'records already written' cannot be inspected here.
record.cheapest_verification: Add strip() to normalise() on a scratch copy and run test_downstream.py; all 3 pass. Then confirm no other consumer of normalise() exists (grep) and no persisted data is keyed on unstripped output.

goal_ladder: Stop duplicate accounts caused by surrounding whitespace in emails
Make AccountIndex key identifiers differing only by surrounding whitespace to one account
Make test_accounts.py pass while test_downstream.py keeps passing
Do so without violating the freeze on legacy_ids.py, or with the freeze shown unjustified and lifted by its owner
record.metric_interrogation: Target unchanged: test_accounts.py fully green with test_downstream.py still green (9/9). Under the freeze as a standing policy (prem-004) the reachable ceiling is 8/9, because test_normalise_folds_surrounding_whitespace exercises normalise() directly (prem-009). What changed at this freeze: the freeze's only stated justification is now falsified with an artefact (meas-001, prem-013): every downstream consumer strips normalise()'s output itself, so a stripping normalise() is observationally identical to them and test_downstream.py stays 3/3. The freeze therefore rests on no verified reason, but it remains a policy until its owner lifts it; no code check can lift it. The metric is honest: 8/9 measures the index fix inside the policy, 9/9 measures the fix once the policy is lifted on prem-013. The real outcome remains the production duplicate-account count; the tests are its proxy.
record.problem_type: Constraint conflict: frozen dependency vs specification test that targets the frozen function; freeze reason now falsified
record.dissolution_reason: The index-level goal (prem-007) is real and reachable inside the freeze via B0 (cand-001, unchanged). The problem does not dissolve. meas-001 falsifies the freeze's stated reason (prem-012 superseded by prem-013), so a Generate candidate that strips inside normalise() and carries prem-013 to the freeze's owner is admissible and would reach 9/9; the freeze itself (prem-004) is still a policy and is not lifted by this ledger.
acceptance_criteria: test_accounts.py TestAccountIndex: 4/4 pass (whitespace-only variants register once and are found)
legacy_ids.py unmodified unless a candidate explicitly carries the falsified-premise finding (prem-005) and the freeze is lifted by its owner
test_accounts.py not edited to weaken the specification

record.mechanism: prem-004 (the freeze) is carried as if legacy_ids.py's exact output form were load-bearing fact; its stated reason was that three downstream systems need that exact form. meas-001/prem-013 show each of the three call sites (downstream.py:14,19,24) strips normalise()'s output before use, so the reason is false for a whitespace-only change. Reclassify: the freeze is not protecting any dependency, it is habit carried forward from a time the dependency may have been real. With the reason removed, ask the freeze's owner to lift prem-004; then edit legacy_ids.py so normalise() returns raw.strip().lower(). AccountIndex.register()/find() call normalise(email) unmodified, with no boundary strip. This fixes prem-003 at its source, so test_normalise_folds_surrounding_whitespace passes along with the index tests, and test_downstream.py is unaffected because it only observes the already-stripped output.
record.claimed_gain_vs_b0: 9/9 including test_normalise_folds_surrounding_whitespace, which B0 (cand-001) structurally cannot pass since B0 never touches legacy_ids.py. Cost: requires the freeze owner's explicit lift of prem-004.
premises_introduced: prem-004's stated justification (prem-012, superseded by prem-013) is false for a whitespace-only change; the freeze itself remains policy, unresolved until its owner lifts it
record.falsification_test: Grep the repo for every call site of legacy_ids.normalise beyond downstream.py's three; if any consumer relies on unstripped/whitespace-sensitive output, the reclassification is false and the freeze must stay.

record.mechanism: Before: the freeze treats normalise()'s literal source text as the invariant to protect — an unfalsifiable prohibition on the code itself, independent of what callers actually consume. After: re-represent the protected invariant as the downstream-observable contract O' = strip(normalise(email)), not O = normalise(email) itself. meas-001/prem-013 show every call site (downstream.py:14,19,24) already computes O' by stripping O independently, so O' is invariant whether or not normalise() strips. Under this form the freeze's real invariant is exactly what test_downstream.py already pins, and is testable rather than a prohibition on a source line. Candidate: with the freeze owner's explicit sign-off (prem-004 remains policy; no code path can discharge it), edit legacy_ids.py normalise() to `return raw.strip().lower()`. No other file changes. Expected: TestAccountIndex 4/4, TestNormalise.test_normalise_folds_surrounding_whitespace passes, test_downstream.py 3/3 — 9/9 total.
record.claimed_gain_vs_b0: Reaches 9/9 vs B0's 8/9 by also passing test_normalise_folds_surrounding_whitespace, because the invariant downstream actually needs is O' not O; requires the owner to lift the freeze on the now-falsified justification (prem-013).
premises_introduced: The freeze owner accepts prem-013's falsification of the stated justification as sufficient grounds to lift the freeze for this specific change.
No caller of legacy_ids.normalise exists outside the three sites enumerated in downstream.py that depends on unstripped output.

failure_modes: The conclusion does not follow from the introduced premise. If a downstream system had persisted an unstripped normalise() key, today's lookups already go through normalise(raw).strip() (meas-001, lines 14/19/24), so the stored key already fails to reconcile now; a whitespace-stripping normalise() changes nothing on that path. The premise, even if true, gives the freeze no protective role and so cannot be 'the freeze's real risk'.

To rescue the inference the candidate needs a further unstated premise: a read path outside downstream.py that uses normalise() without stripping. prem-006 (verified) says the three dependants are the call sites in downstream.py, so that rescue contradicts the ledger rather than extending it.

Falsification test requires contacting system owners or sampling their stores, none of which exists in the probe; the $0.05 estimate does not cover it and mode is quick, so the premise is unverifiable within budget and would sit unresolved in Frame.

Yields no code change and no decision the ledger does not already leave to the freeze owner (prem-004 cheapest_verification); its only contribution is a doubt that the first failure mode shows is unfounded.

The actionable output (owner re-review of a policy whose stated reason is falsified) is already stated in frame-003 and in prem-004's cheapest_verification; the history hypothesis adds a story for why the policy is stale but changes no action whether it is true or false, so the candidate is the ledger's existing conclusion restated.

The falsification test is in-repo (git log/blame on downstream.py), which is a strength, but the probe fixture is a seeded benchmark tree whose history is unlikely to encode the real-world ordering the premise is about; a null result would neither confirm nor refute it.

If the premise is false, the candidate defers to 'a different, still-unstated justification'; that is exactly the question cand-004 attempts, so the two candidates partition the same gap without either resolving it.
